_doc: GUO's own land transition table (docs/data_formats.md §26, 'Transition table'). Authored for GUO; no row comes from Dragon, UO Landscaper or any other map tool. Each pair names an OWNER material (its cells next to the other material are repainted) and an OTHER material. 'edges' gives, per edge shape, the land ids that draw it: a bare id has weight 1, [id, weight] weights a variant. Shapes are named by where the other material lies: N E S W (straight edges), NE SE SW NW (outer corners), in_NE in_SE in_SW in_NW (inner corners, one diagonal neighbour) — EdgeShapes.cs. 'z' is the most an edge cell moves toward the other side's height, per shape, when Land Transitions.EdgeZOffsets is on. 'plain' marks a pair that needs no edge tile at all. 'via' turns an owner cell that faces the other material into the via material when the pair has no tile for it. 'measure' says whether guo-mapgen prepare --measure may add the variants it finds in the user's own client to this pair. Core ids were picked by looking at the art of the user's client and checked against how often Felucca uses them; every id is a land tile number, not art.

resolve._doc: How prepare --measure merges a user's own measurements into the resolved table (UO_MAPGEN_DATA/transitions.guo.resolved.json). A measured variant joins a shape when the pair has min_pair_samples samples, the shape has min_shape_samples and the variant carries min_share of the shape; at most max_variants per shape. Weights come from the measured counts, scaled so the most used variant weighs 'scale'.

Grassland.notes: The common ground. Owns most edges: every other land material is drawn into grass from the grass side.

Forest.notes: Forest floor. Owns its edges to rock, dirt and water.

Beach.notes: Sand. Against water it stays plain sand, as on Felucca; the shoreline reads through the water's height, not through edge tiles.

Mountain.notes: Rock. Never an owner: its neighbours draw the rock edge, raised on the north and west sides.

Swamp.notes: Moss and bog. Only grass and forest blend into it.

Bog.notes: The open bog inside a swamp (0x3DE9-0x3DEC). No biome of its own: Swamp Surface splits each swamp into a moss band and a bog interior.

Water.notes: Never an owner and never painted with an edge tile.

Cobble.notes: Cobblestone streets (RoadPaint.CobbleTiles). Grass and forest meet cobble through their dirt edge.

pairs.notes: Grass fringe over sand, one family 0x33-0x3E. Edge cells sit a little below the grass (about half a z step); flat enough to need no offset.

Rock lip. A land tile is drawn from its own corner and its S/E/SE neighbours' heights, so an edge cell whose rock lies north or west must itself rise to meet it; south- and east-facing edges barely move.
The most common edge in Britannia. Flat. North and east straight edges come in two equal variants.
Flat, family 0xB0-0xC3.
Britannia never lets grass touch snow: rock (or tundra) stands between. A grass cell facing snow becomes rock, which both sides already blend into.
Moss fringe, flat. Straight edges come in two equal variants.

Grass banks straight into water are rare in Britannia and their tiles are mixed; GUO puts a sand cell between, which blends into grass and stands plain against water. If a bank tile is ever drawn, it drops toward the water.
Forest reaches sand through a grass fringe in Britannia (9 direct edges in all of Felucca).
Rock lip, as Grassland>Mountain.
No forest/jungle edge family is in common use; a grass cell between blends into both.
Forest meets swamp through grass in Britannia (63 scattered edges).

Moss band against open bog, drawn by Swamp Surface (Land Transitions never meets Bog). Felucca draws the inner corners with moss tiles whose art carries a dark corner, and 0x3DC2 for the south-west one.
Forest shores go through grass and then sand.
Plain sand against water, as Felucca: no edge tile. Counted as a finished edge, not a hard one.
Jungle fringe over sand, family 0x282-0x28D. Rare in Britannia (under a hundred edges), so the shapes were read from the art.

Rocky shore, where a coast mountain is cut back to sand. Straight edges and outer corners 0x11E-0x129 (the fuller-rock corners 0x122-0x125 weigh double), inner corners 0x7BD-0x7C0, read from the art. Rock lip as Grassland>Mountain, a little higher.
Rock lip, as Grassland>Mountain.
Snow/water family 0x179-0x17B is rare; left to measurement.
Jungle shores go through sand.
Road verge. Flat. Straight edges come in two equal variants.
Forest road verge, flat.
Jungle/dirt family 0x777-0x78C; left to measurement.
Snow road verge, family 0x385-0x390, read from the art (rare in Britannia).
Rare and mixed in Britannia; left to measurement.
Mountain trails: the dirt cell owns the rock edge (Cliff Edge, mountain trails). Rock lip as Grassland>Mountain.
Britannia's streets meet grass through a dirt verge or with mixed tiles (brick, plank, dirt); RoadPaint falls back to Grassland>Dirt.
Too rare to measure.
Cobble street edge on a dirt verge, flat. Road cells are not owners in the generator yet (RoadPaint paints the biome side), so this pair is data for a later street pass.
